title: Why are prices going up?
reason: 昨天的课程讨论聊天机器人与信息判断，今天轮换到金融经济与日常消费。本集用清晰的因果链解释通胀、供应减少、企业成本传导、利率与需求之间的关系，既贴近金融科技业务，也能连接家庭预算和项目成本管理。练习会反复调用六个高频表达，先借助原文完成识别与填空，再逐步用于解释和熟悉的工作场景。

targetExpressions.expression: have a lot to do with
targetExpressions.meaning: be strongly connected with or caused by something
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to explain an important connection: The delay has a lot to do with the supplier change.

targetExpressions.meaning: have less money available because costs have increased
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when a price rise directly affects someone's finances: Commuters are being hit in the pocket by higher fares.

targetExpressions.meaning: be available only in limited quantities
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when demand is greater than the amount available: Skilled engineers can be in short supply during a large migration.

targetExpressions.meaning: make customers pay for additional costs faced by a business
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when a company transfers higher expenses to buyers: The provider may pass on the extra costs through higher fees.

targetExpressions.meaning: make someone less willing or less likely to do an action
targetExpressions.usage: Use discourage + person + from + -ing: Higher interest rates can discourage businesses from borrowing.
Use it after an explanation or for a sensible decision: The pricing change makes sense when the higher costs are included.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Beth's explanation: Our money buying less these days ______ inflation.
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: have a lot to do with
answers: has a lot to do with
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Beth says the reduced buying power of money has a lot to do with inflation, the increase in prices over time.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the description of consumers: Rising prices mean that people are being ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript defines being hit in the pocket as having less money to spend.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What usually happens to prices when essential goods are in short supply?

options.text: They rise because only limited quantities are available.
They fall because every consumer stops needing the goods.
They stay fixed because supply cannot affect prices.
They disappear from company accounts but not from shops.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme explains that reduced supply of necessary goods contributed to price rises; in short supply means available in limited quantities.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the explanation: Companies may ______ by charging more for their goods and services.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript says companies can pass on costs they have already faced by increasing what customers pay.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the policy effect using the target pattern: Higher interest rates can ______ people ______ borrowing.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Vicky Pryce explains that increasing interest rates discourages individuals and businesses from borrowing.

options.text: The explanation makes sense because lower borrowing can reduce demand.
The explanation makes a sense about borrowing.
The bank made sense the interest rate yesterday.
Demand was make sense by the customer.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Make sense means be logical or understandable and does not take an article or a direct object in this use.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Why might inflation continue even if food and energy prices later come down?

options.text: Companies may still pass on costs they have already faced through higher prices.
Consumers immediately borrow more whenever energy becomes cheaper.
Developing economies stop producing all goods when prices fall.
Interest rates automatically become fees paid directly to shops.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Linda Yueh says sustained increases can enter company pricing, so businesses may pass on costs already incurred even after volatile input prices decline.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which chain correctly summarises the programme's explanation of higher interest rates?

options.text: They discourage borrowing, which can reduce buying and slow demand.
They encourage borrowing, which immediately removes inflation.
They increase the supply of food without affecting demand.
They guarantee higher incomes while production falls.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The economist's causal chain is higher interest rates, less borrowing, fewer purchases and slower demand, which can help control inflation.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80–120 words using this structure: (1) topic—what inflation is and how it affects consumers; (2) causes—reduced supply and company costs; (3) response—how higher interest rates may slow demand. Phrase bank: “be hit in the pocket”, “be in short supply”, “pass on the extra costs”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate sentences are enough.
referencePoints: Inflation means prices increase over time, so consumers have less money to spend and are hit in the pocket.
Food and energy prices were rising, while the pandemic and the war in Ukraine reduced supplies of necessary goods.
When goods are in short supply, limited availability can push their prices upward.
Sustained increases can enter company pricing, and businesses may pass on costs they have already faced.
A recession involves falling production and incomes together with rising unemployment.
Higher interest rates discourage borrowing, which can reduce purchases and slow demand to help control inflation.
